title: Looking Up Keys
goal: In this lesson you will learn how to look up a value with square brackets and a key.
learn: Print values one at a time
Mix looked-up values in one print
idea: To get a value, put the key in square brackets: pet["name"]. Python finds that key and gives you its value. If you mistype the key, you get an error. So spell keys carefully!
changeOneLine: In the editor above, change the first print to pet["type"]. Press Run. The first line should say cat.

practice.text: Print the book title and pages using key lookups.
practice.hint: Use square brackets with the key inside quotes: book["title"] and book["pages"]. One print per value.
practice.starterTip: First line: print(book["title"]). Second: print(book["pages"]). You should see Wonder and 310.
practice.gradingNote: Pass if two prints look up book["title"] and book["pages"] and show Wonder and 310.

practice.text: Print a sentence like Cookie costs 2 using snack keys.
practice.hint: Look up snack["name"] and snack["cost"] inside one print(). You can mix words in quotes with the looked-up values.
practice.starterTip: Try print(snack["name"], "costs", snack["cost"]). That prints Cookie costs 2.
practice.gradingNote: Pass if one print uses snack keys to show Cookie and 2.

quiz.question: If pet = {"name": "Mochi"}, what does pet["name"] give you?
quiz.correct: Square brackets with a key look up that key's value.

quiz.question: What happens if you look up a key that is not there?
quiz.correct: A missing key causes a KeyError (until you learn safer tools).

quiz.question: Which line looks up the level?
quiz.correct: Use square brackets and the key string.
quiz.wrong: Dictionary lookup uses ["key"], not a bare word.

project.title: Pet Lookups
project.desc: Print name, type, and age on separate lines, then one sentence using all three keys.
project.starter:
pet = {"name": "Buddy", "type": "dog", "age": 5}
print("Name:", pet["name"])
print()
print()
